litigation.note: The Corporate Governance Report ('Details of non-compliance, penalties, strictures imposed') discloses that during FY 2025-26 the Regional Director (North Western Region), Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Ahmedabad, vide Interim Order dated 04 July 2025 under Section 441 of the Companies Act, 2013, compounded a default relating to non-disclosure of the reasons for non-spending of the prescribed CSR amount in the Board's Report for FY 2017-18, a contravention of Section 134(3)(o) read with Section 135. A compounding fee was imposed on the Company and separately on Mr. Rahul Mangal, Director, and Mr. Ashish Mangal, Director (amounts deliberately not reproduced here). The Company states it complied with the order and paid the compounding fees within the prescribed time, and that the order has no material impact on going-concern status or future operations. Stated absences elsewhere in the routed text: no equity shares in the demat suspense account; no amount liable to be transferred to the IEPF; no whistle-blower event reported and no personnel denied access to the Audit Committee during FY 2025-26; nil POSH complaints filed, disposed, pending or pending over 90 days; no loans/advances to firms/companies in which directors are interested; no audit qualification on the financial statements; no contracts or arrangements not at arm's length; no agreements impacting management or control. The Form AOC-2 arm's-length table is printed entirely as '-' (stated nil). No other litigation, contingent-liability or claim narrative appears in the routed profile text.

risks.note: Stated as fluctuations that 'may impact margins and profitability'; mitigated by strategic procurement, inventory planning, diversified sourcing and operational efficiencies. This is the risk that actually MATERIALISED in FY26: both leadership letters describe a sharp correction in CRGO steel prices that hit industry realisations, and the MD&A attributes the margin compression to lower CRGO realisations despite healthy volume growth. Structurally the business is a CRGO processor, so realisation follows the steel price while volume follows grid capex — the two can diverge.
risks.risk: Raw material price volatility — CRGO, CRNO and other key inputs

risks.note: Stated as 'delays in commissioning new manufacturing facilities or scaling operations could affect future growth plans'; mitigated by structured project execution, phased capacity expansion and continuous monitoring of project milestones. Load-bearing here because the greenfield 220kV/100 MVA transformer facility is the Company's main growth lever and the AR gives it no commissioning date, ramp schedule or cost.

Stated as 'revenue is dependent on continued business from key customers across the power infrastructure sector'; mitigated by long-standing relationships, a diversified customer base and expansion into new customer segments. The AR does NOT quantify the concentration — no top-customer or top-10 share of revenue is disclosed anywhere in the routed text, so the magnitude of this risk is unknown rather than nil.

Stated as competition that 'may lead to pricing pressure and market share challenges'; mitigated by quality, technical approvals, integrated manufacturing and customer service. Already visible in FY26: the MD&A cites intensified competition in the transformer business exerting pressure on pricing and profitability.
risks.risk: Industry competition from organised and unorganised players

risks.note: Stated as changes in government policies, environmental regulations or industry standards that may impact operations; mitigated by continuous regulatory monitoring, a compliance framework and adherence to industry standards. Structurally amplified by the customer mix — government utilities and DISCOMs — and by demand that depends on state transmission/distribution capex programmes.

Stated as 'imports of raw materials and export revenues expose the Company to currency fluctuations'; mitigated through prudent treasury practices, periodic review of exposures and 'appropriate hedging strategies' — the sentence is TRUNCATED mid-clause in the source, so the full mitigation and any hedging policy detail are not readable. Note the Corporate Governance Report separately states the Company 'does not deal in commodities' so the SEBI commodity-price-risk disclosure is not required, and refers the reader to the MD&A for FX and hedging — i.e. this truncated row is the only FX disclosure there is.

The cautionary statement names, as factors that could make actual results differ, 'economic conditions affecting demand, supply, and price conditions in the domestic & overseas markets in which the Company operates, changes in Government regulations, tax laws & other statutes'. The whole investment case in the MD&A rests on third-party projections (National Electricity Plan transmission investment by 2032, 500 GW non-fossil capacity by 2030, ~8.2% transformer-market CAGR 2026-2031), none of which is a company order book — see the note on the absent order-book disclosure.
risks.risk: Demand / macro dependence on the domestic and overseas power capex cycle

sk.overview: Powerica operates across two industries: (1) India's standby power / diesel-generator (DG set) market, where DG sets, UPS, inverters and battery storage provide backup power during outages/voltage fluctuations across commercial, manufacturing, IT/data-centre, telecom and infrastructure sectors (F&S Report); and (2) India's wind power sector within the broader renewable energy industry, where wind plays a pivotal role in the country's energy transition (CRISIL Report).
